title: First Bad Version
summary: An app has versions numbered 1 to n, each built on top of the one before. At some point a bug slipped in: the version that introduced it and every version after it are bad, while all earlier versions are good. A helper `isBadVersion(v)` tells you whether version v is bad, but each call is slow. Return the first bad version, calling the helper as few times as possible.

examples.explanation: Version 5 is still good and version 6 is bad, so the bug came in with version 6.
The bug was there from the very first version.

constraints: The last version, n, is always bad

approaches.twist: Search for the first bad version: if the middle version is bad, keep it and look left; if it's good, look right of it.
Check versions 1, 2, 3 and so on in order, and return the first one the helper calls bad.
approaches.note: Works, but it may call the helper once per version, and n can be about 2·10⁹. The target is O(log n) calls.

signals.meaning: The versions run good, good, …, bad, bad: the answer flips only once, so checking a middle version tells you which side of it the first bad one is on.
You aren't matching a value; you're looking for the boundary where good turns bad. A bad middle version could be that boundary, so it stays in the range.
Checking versions one by one could take n calls, and n can be about 2·10⁹. Halving the range needs at most 31.

constraintReading: n can be 2³¹ − 1, about 2.1·10⁹, so checking versions in order could mean billions of slow calls: O(n) is ruled out. Halving the range needs at most 31 calls, O(log n), with O(1) space for lo and hi.

related.relation: Also looks for the first position where a test passes, and lo ends right on it.
